findings.title: Reentrancy guard cleared before hook fee external calls in queue executor
findings.description: _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) is called at line 3190 before the loop of external hook fee transfer calls. During those external calls, any smart contract recipient can re-enter the AMM with no guard set.
findings.impact: Hook fee recipient could drain additional fees or manipulate AMM state during unguarded re-entry
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Execute swap with hook that queues fee to a malicious recipient. 2. executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers clears flags at line 3190. 3. Malicious recipient's receive() re-enters AMM. 4. No reentrancy guard is set at this point.

findings.title: SingleProviderPoolType state write after external hook call
findings.description: Both swap functions call ILimitBreakAMM(AMM).getPoolState(), then ISingleProviderPoolHook(poolHook).getPoolPriceForSwap() (user-controlled contract), then write pools[poolId].lastSqrtPriceX96. Aderyn flagged as H-1. A malicious hook could re-enter the AMM during price retrieval and manipulate the price cache.
findings.impact: Price manipulation via malicious hook re-entering AMM during getPoolPriceForSwap callback
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Deploy malicious hook. 2. Hook re-enters AMM during getPoolPriceForSwap. 3. AMM state changes before lastSqrtPriceX96 is written. 4. Stale price cached.

findings.title: balanceInBefore stale after ETH refund via _depositWrappedNativeAndRefundExcess
findings.description: After _depositWrappedNativeAndRefundExcess sends ETH back to executor via .call (which triggers executor's fallback), the AMM checks balanceInBefore + amountIn == balanceInAfter. If executor's fallback re-enters with a different swap, balanceInBefore was read before the re-entrant call mutated the balance. Reentrancy guard should block this but warrants verification.
findings.impact: Stale balance check could allow double-counting of deposited funds
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Call swap with msg.value. 2. ETH refund triggers executor fallback. 3. Fallback re-enters AMM. 4. balanceInBefore is stale from before refund call.

findings.title: computeRatioX96 overflow returns 0 enabling max-bound bypass in validateHandlerOrder
findings.description: When amount1 * multiplier overflows in computeRatioX96, the function returns 0. In validateHandlerOrder, sqrtPriceX96 of 0 silently bypasses the max-bound check (0 > maxSqrtPriceX96 is always false). This allows CLOB orders to be placed above the token creator's maximum price bound.
findings.impact: CLOB orders placed above maximum price bound set by token creator
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Find sqrtPriceX96 values causing overflow in computeRatioX96. 2. Function returns 0. 3. validateHandlerOrder checks 0 > maxSqrtPriceX96 = false. 4. Max-bound bypassed.

findings.title: FixedHelper withdrawLiquidity bitwise OR operator precedence bug
findings.description: if (redeposited0 | redeposited1 == 0) uses bitwise OR, not logical OR — only reverts if BOTH are zero. Operator precedence: | has lower precedence than ==, so this parses as redeposited0 | (redeposited1 == 0). If exactly one side is zero and the other is non-zero, the unchecked subtraction on line 74 proceeds.
findings.impact: Potential underflow in unchecked subtraction when one redeposited value is zero
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Call withdrawLiquidity where redeposited0=0, redeposited1>0. 2. Check parses as 0 | (redeposited1 == 0) = 0 | false = 0. 3. Revert triggers. But if redeposited0>0, redeposited1=0: redeposited0 | (0 == 0) = redeposited0 | 1 = nonzero. 4. No revert, unchecked subtraction proceeds.

findings.title: setTokenSettings makes external call before state write (CEI violation)
findings.description: hookFlags() external call on untrusted hook contract occurs before tokenSettings storage write. A malicious hook could re-enter other AMM functions that read partially-written token settings.
findings.impact: Partial token settings state could be read by re-entered functions, enabling misconfigured hook enforcement
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Deploy malicious hook whose hookFlags() re-enters createPool or addLiquidity. 2. Call setTokenSettings(token, maliciousHook, flags). 3. hookFlags() triggers re-entry. 4. Re-entered function reads stale tokenSettings.

findings.title: afterSwapRefund lacks nonReentrant and calls WRAPPED_NATIVE.withdrawToAccount with ETH callback
findings.description: afterSwapRefund lacks nonReentrant and calls WRAPPED_NATIVE.withdrawToAccount which can trigger ETH callbacks to attacker contracts. If the AMM clears its reentrancy guard before executing post-swap callbacks, re-entry to CLOB openOrder/withdrawToken is possible.
findings.impact: Potential re-entry to CLOB functions during post-swap ETH refund callback
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Execute swap triggering afterSwapRefund. 2. withdrawToAccount sends ETH to attacker. 3. Attacker fallback re-enters CLOB. 4. Check if AMM reentrancy guard is cleared by this point.

findings.title: FixedHelper _splitAmountsAndFeesByHeight highest complexity rounding
findings.description: Highest cyclomatic complexity function (20). Multi-pass rounding corrections, +1 allowance at line 1680, unchecked arithmetic in excess-fee path. Divide-before-multiply in height traversal loops (Slither IDs 5/6).
findings.impact: Rounding errors accumulating across multiple height levels could lead to value extraction
findings.proof_sketch: Fuzz with extreme height counts and small amounts to find rounding discrepancies.

findings.title: DynamicPoolType has no onlyAMM access control guard
findings.description: Unlike FixedPoolType and SingleProviderPoolType which enforce onlyAMM, DynamicPoolType has zero access control on all external state-mutating functions. Storage is namespaced by msg.sender (globalState[msg.sender]), so direct callers write to their own namespace. Critical question: does AMMModule dispatch via delegatecall (preserving msg.sender=AMM, making this correct) or external call? NOTE: Cross-contract-tracer confirmed external call pattern (not delegatecall). Namespace-by-sender isolates pools; direct callers only write to their own namespace. Severity reduced.
findings.impact: If external call: any caller can interact with pool type state using any address as the AMM key
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Check AMMModule dispatch mechanism to pool types. 2. If external call, msg.sender = AMM address. 3. If delegatecall, msg.sender preserved. 4. Verify namespace isolation under both models.

findings.title: SecureProxy pause code replay after admin pause clear
findings.description: After secureAdminPause(true) clears a pause, already-used Tier 1 codes are consumed but any unused Tier 1 codes in a valid code set can trigger another pause.
findings.impact: Griefing: protocol repeatedly paused using revealed codes, disrupting operations for up to 30 min intervals
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Attacker observes Tier 1 code used on-chain. 2. Admin clears pause. 3. Another unused Tier 1 code from same set replayed. 4. Protocol paused again.

findings.title: Flash loan fee token from hook enables balance check manipulation
findings.description: The hook can return an arbitrary feeToken. Fee-on-transfer or rebasing tokens as feeToken would cause requiredFeeTokenBalanceAfter to be computed incorrectly. NOTE: feeToken is admin-configured via hook, not attacker-controlled; severity reduced.
findings.impact: Flash loan fee bypass: attacker borrows tokens paying insufficient fees
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Set up token hook that returns a fee-on-transfer token as feeToken. 2. Execute flashLoan. 3. Balance check uses static snapshot but fee-on-transfer token loses value during transfer.

findings.title: _safeDecrementUint128 does not check uint128 truncation
findings.description: The assembly only checks gt(difference, a) to catch underflow, but does not verify difference <= type(uint128).max.
findings.impact: Silent truncation of fee or reserve values
findings.proof_sketch: Find path where _safeDecrementUint128 is called with a > type(uint128).max.
